source.title: Look-alike questions the profile cannot or must not answer

questions.label: Do you currently receive SNAP benefits?
questions.note: Asks whether SNAP is received now; the profile only knows whether the applicant is applying.

questions.label: Is anyone in your household currently getting food stamps?
questions.note: Current SNAP receipt, not an application; the profile does not save it.

questions.label: Are you enrolled in WIC?
questions.note: WIC enrollment is not in the profile.

questions.label: Do you currently have Medicaid?
questions.note: Current Medicaid coverage, not applying for it; the profile does not save it.

questions.label: Does your household receive TANF or FIP cash assistance right now?
questions.note: Cash assistance received now, not an application; the profile does not save it.

questions.label: Does anyone in your household receive SSI or SSDI?
questions.note: Disability benefits received; having a disability does not mean getting SSI or SSDI.

questions.label: Has your SNAP application been approved?
questions.note: The status of an earlier application is not in the profile.

questions.label: Have you applied for SNAP in the past 12 months?
questions.note: Past applications are not in the profile; applyingSnap only covers applying now.

questions.label: Were you denied SNAP benefits in the last year?
questions.note: Past SNAP decisions are not in the profile.

questions.label: Do your children get free or reduced-price school meals?
questions.note: School meal benefits are not in the profile.

questions.label: Do you receive Social Security benefits?
questions.note: Income sources are not saved, only monthly totals.

questions.label: Does anyone in the household receive unemployment benefits?
questions.note: Income sources are not saved, only monthly totals.

questions.label: Does anyone in your household receive VA benefits?
questions.note: VA benefits are not saved; a veteran in the household may or may not get them.

questions.label: Do you have health insurance?
questions.note: Health insurance coverage is not in the profile.

questions.label: Would you like information about applying for SNAP?
questions.note: A request for information, not whether the applicant is applying.

questions.label: Would you like someone to contact you about Medicaid?
questions.note: A contact preference, not an application for Medicaid.

questions.label: Medicare/Medicaid
questions.note: One box for two different programs, and it does not say whether it means having them or applying.

questions.label: Programs you currently receive (check all that apply)
questions.note: Programs received now, several at once; the yes/no rules cannot pick from this list.

questions.label: How many people in your household are 18-59?
questions.note: The profile counts adults 18-64; anyone 60-64 makes the 18-59 count unknown.

questions.label: How many household members are age 60 or older?
questions.note: The profile counts people 65+, not 60+.

questions.label: Anyone in your household under age 5?
questions.note: The profile counts children under 18, not under 5.

questions.label: Are there children under 6 in the home?
questions.note: The profile counts children under 18, not under 6.

questions.label: How many children ages 0-5?
questions.note: The profile counts children under 18, not 0-5.

questions.label: Number of household members ages 6-17
questions.note: The profile counts all children under 18 together, not ages 6-17.

questions.label: How many adults 18 and older live in your household?
questions.note: 18 and older includes seniors 65+; the profile counts adults 18-64 and seniors separately, so this band is not one of its counts.

questions.label: Number of adults (19-59)
questions.note: Band 19-59 does not match the profile, which counts adults 18-64.

questions.label: Are there any grandparents raising grandchildren in your household?
questions.note: Family relationships are not in the profile.

questions.label: Are there any teenagers (13-17) in your household?
questions.note: The profile does not know children’s ages, only how many are under 18.

questions.label: How many infants (under 1 year) live with you?
questions.note: The profile does not count infants.

questions.label: Are you over 60?
questions.note: “Over 60” could mean 60 and up or 61 and up; for someone exactly 60 the answer depends on the reading.

questions.label: Is anyone in the household over 65?
questions.note: “Over 65” could mean 65 and up or 66 and up; the profile counts people 65 and older.

questions.label: Does your household include a senior citizen?
questions.note: “Senior” has no age here; pantries use 55, 60 or 65.

questions.label: Is anyone in your household elderly?
questions.note: No age is given for elderly.

questions.label: Do you have kids?
questions.note: Does not say under 18 or living in the household; grown children or children elsewhere would count.

questions.label: Do you have children in school?
questions.note: School enrollment is not in the profile.

questions.label: Is anyone in your household a full-time student?
questions.note: Student status is not in the profile.

questions.label: Age of youngest child
questions.note: Children’s ages are not in the profile, and the range options would wrongly match the applicant’s age.

questions.label: How many seniors (60+) live with you?
questions.note: The profile counts people 65+, not 60+.

questions.label: How many people in your household are 60-64?
questions.note: The profile does not split adults 18-64 by age.

questions.label: What year were you born?
questions.note: Birth years, not ages; the age-range rule would wrongly compare the applicant’s age to these numbers.

questions.label: Are you a veteran?
questions.note: Asks about the applicant only; the veteran fact covers the whole household.

questions.label: Are you currently serving in the military?
questions.note: Asks about the applicant’s active duty now; the profile knows only whether someone in the household is a veteran or in the military.

questions.label: Do you have a disability?
questions.note: Asks about the applicant only; the disability fact covers the whole household.

questions.label: Are you pregnant or breastfeeding?
questions.note: Applicant only, and breastfeeding is not in the profile.

questions.label: Are you a U.S. citizen?
questions.note: Asks about the applicant only; the profile knows whether everyone in the household is a citizen.

questions.label: Are you enrolled in Medicare?
questions.note: Asks about the applicant only; the Medicare fact covers the whole household.

questions.label: Is anyone in your household pregnant or breastfeeding?
questions.note: Breastfeeding is not in the profile, so a No cannot be proven.

questions.label: Is anyone in your household the surviving spouse of a veteran?
questions.note: Surviving spouses are not in the profile.

questions.label: Does anyone in your household have a disability that keeps them from working?
questions.note: Narrower than having a disability; the profile does not know about work limits.

questions.label: Is anyone in the household blind or deaf?
questions.note: A specific disability; the profile only knows whether anyone has a disability.

questions.label: Is anyone in your household a lawful permanent resident (green card holder)?
questions.note: Immigration status of non-citizens is not saved this way.

questions.label: Were all household members born in the United States?
questions.note: Place of birth is not in the profile; citizens can be born abroad.

questions.label: Is everyone in your household a U.S. citizen or qualified non-citizen?
questions.note: Includes qualified non-citizens, so it is broader than the all-citizens fact.

questions.label: Military status
questions.note: The applicant’s own status among several choices; the veteran fact is a household yes/no.

questions.label: Are you a student?
questions.note: Student status is not in the profile.

questions.label: Are you enrolled in college at least half time?
questions.note: Student status is not in the profile.

questions.label: Are you currently employed?
questions.note: Employment is not saved; the profile has income amounts only.

questions.label: Is anyone in your household working?
questions.note: Employment is not saved; earned income could come from past work or self-employment.

questions.label: Are you retired?
questions.note: Retirement is not in the profile.

questions.label: Do you rent or own your home?
questions.note: Housing type is not saved; the profile knows only rent cost and whether there is a home address.

questions.label: Are you at risk of losing your housing?
questions.note: Housing risk is not in the profile.

questions.label: Are you homeless or at risk of homelessness?
questions.note: At risk of homelessness is broader than having no home address.

questions.label: Are you staying in a shelter?
questions.note: Shelter stays are not saved; the profile only knows whether there is a home address.

questions.label: Do you live in public or subsidized housing?
questions.note: Housing type is not in the profile.

questions.label: Housing status
questions.note: Several housing types; the homeless rule is yes/no.

questions.label: Have you moved in the last 12 months?
questions.note: Moves are not in the profile.

questions.label: Do you have access to a kitchen to cook meals?
questions.note: Kitchen access is not in the profile.

questions.label: Do you have a working stove and refrigerator?
questions.note: Appliances are not in the profile.

questions.label: Do you pay heating or cooling costs separately from rent?
questions.note: The profile has a utilities total but not which costs are separate from rent.

questions.label: Do you live in our service area?
questions.note: The service area is not stated, so it cannot be checked against the address.

questions.label: Do you live within Des Moines city limits?
questions.note: City limits are narrower than the saved city name; there is no city rule.

questions.label: Do you live in Polk, Dallas, or Warren County?
questions.note: Asks about three counties at once; the county rule checks one.

questions.label: Have you lived in Iowa for at least 30 days?
questions.note: How long the applicant has lived in the state is not saved.

questions.label: Do you intend to stay in Iowa?
questions.note: Plans to stay are not in the profile.

questions.label: Which ZIP code do you live in?
questions.note: A list of ZIP codes; no answer rule picks a ZIP from choices.

questions.label: Which neighborhood do you live in?
questions.note: Neighborhoods are not in the profile.

questions.label: Is your mailing address different from your home address?
questions.note: Mailing addresses are not compared in the facts.

questions.label: Which pantry location is closest to you?
questions.note: Pantry sites are not in the profile.

questions.label: Do you live on campus?
questions.note: Campus housing is not in the profile.

questions.label: Mailing address: State
questions.note: The mailing address may differ from where the applicant lives; the state fact is the home state.

questions.label: What state were you born in?
questions.note: Place of birth, not the state the applicant lives in.

questions.label: Monthly income (circle one: weekly / monthly)
questions.note: Which period the written income is for; the applicant’s choice.

questions.label: Is your household income at or below 185% of the federal poverty guidelines?
questions.note: The limit depends on household size and the current guideline table.

questions.label: Is your household’s income below the amount shown for your household size in the chart above?
questions.note: Income table by household size; the amount is not in the question.

questions.label: Is your weekly household income less than $500?
questions.note: Weekly income cannot be worked out exactly from a monthly total.

questions.label: How often are you paid?
questions.note: Pay frequency is not in the profile.

questions.label: Has your income changed in the last 30 days?
questions.note: Income changes are not in the profile.

questions.label: Has anyone in your household lost a job in the last 60 days?
questions.note: Job loss is not in the profile.

questions.label: Main source of household income
questions.note: Income sources are not saved, only amounts.

questions.label: Does your household have less than $100 in cash, checking, and savings?
questions.note: Asks about savings, not income; no answer rule compares savings to an amount.

questions.label: Does anyone in your household earn more than $1,000 a month from a job?
questions.note: About one person’s wages; the profile has household totals only.

questions.label: Weekly household income
questions.note: Weekly ranges; the income-range rule only handles month or year.

questions.label: Is your household income more than $3,000 a month?
questions.note: Asks whether income is above the amount; the income rule answers below, so its Yes would be wrong here.

questions.label: Total household income last year (from your tax return)
questions.note: Last year’s taxed income may differ from the current monthly income times 12.

questions.label: Do you pay child support?
questions.note: Child support payments are not in the profile.

questions.label: Do you pay for child care so you can work or go to school?
questions.note: Child care costs are not in the profile.

questions.label: Do you receive help paying your rent?
questions.note: Rent help is not in the profile.

questions.label: Have you received a utility shut-off notice?
questions.note: Shut-off notices are not in the profile.

questions.label: Preferred pickup day
questions.note: Pickup preference.

questions.label: Preferred pickup time
questions.note: Pickup preference; the times are not ranges of a saved value.

questions.label: Is this your first visit to our pantry?
questions.note: Visit history is not in the profile.

questions.label: How did you hear about us?
questions.note: How they heard about the pantry.

questions.label: Would you like your food delivered?
questions.note: Delivery preference.

questions.label: Do you need an interpreter?
questions.note: Language needs are not in the profile.

questions.label: Preferred language
questions.note: Language is not in the profile.

questions.label: Do you or anyone in your household have food allergies?
questions.note: Allergies are not in the profile.

questions.label: Does anyone in your household follow a special diet (diabetic, low sodium, halal, kosher)?
questions.note: Dietary needs are not in the profile.

questions.label: Do you have any pets?
questions.note: Pets are not in the profile.

questions.label: Do you need baby formula or diapers?
questions.note: A request for baby items; children under 18 do not tell whether there is a baby.

questions.label: Do you have reliable transportation to the pantry?
questions.note: Transportation is not in the profile.

questions.label: Will someone else pick up food for you?
questions.note: Proxy pickup is not in the profile.

questions.label: How many times have you visited a food pantry this month?
questions.note: Visit counts are not in the profile; the options only look like household counts.

questions.label: How many bags of food do you need?
questions.note: A request, not a household count.

questions.label: How many people will come with you to pick up?
questions.note: Not a household count.

questions.label: How many meals a day do you usually eat?
questions.note: Meals are not in the profile.

questions.label: How many bedrooms are in your home?
questions.note: Bedrooms are not in the profile.

questions.label: How many people in your household are employed?
questions.note: Employment is not in the profile.

questions.label: How many pets live in your home?
questions.note: Pets are not in the profile.

questions.label: Number of vehicles your household owns
questions.note: Vehicles are not in the profile.

questions.label: How many people in your household besides yourself?
questions.note: Counts everyone except the applicant; picking the household size would be off by one.

questions.label: How long have you lived at your current address?
questions.note: Time at the address is not in the profile; the year ranges would wrongly match the applicant’s age.

questions.label: How many years have you lived in the United States?
questions.note: Years in the US are not in the profile.

questions.label: Gender
questions.note: Gender is not in the profile.

questions.label: Race (check all that apply)
questions.note: Race is not in the profile.

questions.label: Marital status
questions.note: Marital status is not in the profile.

questions.label: Highest level of education completed
questions.note: Education is not in the profile.

questions.label: In the past 12 months, did you worry your food would run out before you had money to buy more?
questions.note: Food security screener; not in the profile.

questions.label: I certify that the information I have given is true and correct.
questions.note: Attestation; only the applicant can make it.

questions.label: I agree to the pantry’s terms and conditions.
questions.note: Agreeing to terms is the applicant’s decision.

questions.label: Signature
questions.note: The applicant signs.

questions.label: Date
questions.note: The date written beside the signature.

questions.label: Social Security Number
questions.note: SecondHand never fills in a Social Security number.

questions.label: Last 4 digits of your SSN
questions.note: Part of the Social Security number; never filled in.

questions.label: Would you like to register to vote?
questions.note: Registering to vote is the applicant’s own decision.

questions.label: May we share your information with our partner agencies?
questions.note: Consent to share information.

questions.label: Do you agree to receive text messages from the pantry?
questions.note: Consent to texts is the applicant’s choice.

questions.label: I understand that giving false information may result in losing benefits.
questions.note: Acknowledgment only the applicant can give.

questions.label: By checking this box, I confirm I have read the privacy notice.
options: I have read the privacy notice
questions.note: Acknowledgment only the applicant can give.

questions.label: Type your full name as your electronic signature
questions.note: An electronic signature, even though it is the applicant’s name.

questions.label: Do you give us permission to verify your income with your employer?
questions.note: Consent to verification.

questions.label: I declare under penalty of perjury that my household’s income is at or below the limit shown above.
questions.note: A sworn statement about income; only the applicant can make it.

questions.label: I certify that my household lives in Iowa.
questions.note: A certification, not a question; the applicant must make it.

questions.label: Would you like to receive our newsletter and updates?
questions.note: Opting in to mailings is the applicant’s choice.

questions.label: May we contact you later for a follow-up survey?
questions.note: Consent to be contacted.

questions.label: Do you give permission for us to take and use photos of you at distributions?
questions.note: Photo consent.

questions.label: Social Security numbers of all household members
questions.note: Social Security numbers are never filled in.

questions.label: Signature of head of household or authorized representative
questions.note: Signature.
